title: How to Get a Yes From Anyone (and Change Your Life)
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: Guest promoting new edition of his book How to Get a Meeting with Anyone.

stated_problem.quote: if you go through usual channels and you do the usual things, that is not the way you stand out.
stated_problem.speaker: Stu Heinecke

idea.name: Personalized cartoon contact-marketing campaigns
idea.one_liner: Highly personalized outreach to a top-100 list of high-value targets using custom cartoons (recipient out of frame, complimentary humour) on mailers, big foam boards and windowed FedEx envelopes

key_quotes.quote: A big feature of contact marketing is it's not mass marketing at all.
So the metrics that I've seen in contact marketing, they easily hit 100% response rates.
you hand make a cartoon and but you have AI plug in thousands or hundreds or dozens of different variables that make it custom to each person

claims.quote: so, you know, my first contact campaign did that.
the highest response rate that I'm aware of and ROI that I'm aware of are let's say for response rate it's somewhere north of 300%.

acquisition_channels.details: personalized cartoon mailings, 18x24in foam boards, FedEx window envelopes

ideas.delivery: Professional cartoonists (Playboy/New Yorker) plus personalization research; AI can scale variables

idea.name: Tongue scraper brand landing Walmart via $28 geo-targeted ad
idea.one_liner: Dentist-invented tongue scraper sold via YouTube, then a $28 Facebook ad targeted at Walmart HQ in Bentonville produced a $2M order

key_quotes.quote: So they put together a little just a little tiny Facebook ad, static Facebook ad, paid $28 for it.

claims.quote: And they exited that conversation with a 20, what was it? No, $2 million order.
2 million be going before going into that conversation and then 10xed to 20 million.

acquisition_channels.details: geo-targeted Facebook ad at retailer HQ

stated_problem.quote: and they don't sell online and they have this huge billion-dollar brand.
stated_problem.speaker: Chris Koerner

idea.name: Unofficial online reseller of Buc-ee's merchandise
idea.one_liner: Buy one of everything from a brand that doesn't sell online and resell online, launched with cold emails to reporters

key_quotes.quote: It cost $1,500 and I launched a business and I cold emailed 20 reporters.

claims.claim: Millions a year after five years
claims.quote: it's been five years since that business and we do millions of dollars a year and we sell all of Buckyy's products online unofficially.

uk_legal_risk.reason: Reselling genuine goods is lawful (exhaustion of rights) but avoid implying official affiliation/trademark misuse

idea.name: Trigger-based commercial tenant-rep outreach
idea.one_liner: Commercial realtor watches lease records/news of new store openings and sends a laminated framed news article with a note to win the next lease

key_quotes.quote: He spent half hour of his time, $10 in materials to handel that to me for $9,000 in my next lease.

claims.quote: That's $180,000. He's going to get about 5% of that.

stated_problem.quote: before that, there was no way to buy a list of companies that were in trouble.
stated_problem.speaker: Stu Heinecke

idea.name: Turnaround consultancy with Gladiator-sword outreach
idea.one_liner: Scan business news for missed earnings, send CEO a $1,000 engraved sword with handwritten note offering turnaround help

key_quotes.quote: he scan the business news every morning looking for stories of missed earnings estimates.

claims.quote: But still, when he does engage that, the engagements are worth a million and up.
Do you know what they cost to make? About $1,000.

acquisition_channels.details: engraved sword in box with handwritten note

idea.name: Prospecting book How to Get a Meeting with Anyone
idea.one_liner: Bestselling sales book on contact marketing, new AI-era edition

key_quotes.quote: Last year, it was named the number one sales book ever written on prospecting by Sales Daily.
